image_prompt.text: Several dense forests of ultra-realistic 3D vegetation covering the map - layered canopy, undergrowth, ferns and fallen trunks - with natural clearings and animal trails threading between them
Several wide rivers winding across the map, clear enough to see the bed, deep enough for animals to swim, and wide enough to separate one stretch of forest from the next
Natural dens and nests under the forest cover - hollow logs, riverbank burrows, rock hollows - that animal players claim and return to
One towering natural landmark standing above the canopy and visible from across the map, so players can navigate the forest by sight
A wide clearing at a river bend where many animals can gather at once, sized for a crowd without crowding the bank

mechanics: Several animals the player can control, switching between them
Ultra-realistic walking and running animation for the animals
On-screen joystick plus run, hit and jump buttons (mobile-first controls)
notes: preset Animal Sim taken whole; its wilderness-open shape already matches the gigantic natural map, so no shape substitution was needed
water-body routes CHECK: the rivers read as a surface with a swim envelope over it, which is only a problem if the play volume self-occludes

forests and vegetation shipped as free text with no ID - no catalogue option covers vegetation cover. zone-graphics was rejected because the foliage here is the whole world rather than an isolated detail cluster set aside from the route

extent vs detail: a gigantic multi-forest world framed in one isometric render comes back as canopy and river courses, not per-animal realism. Built as one continuous map as asked; a per-region decomposition (P4) is the alternative if close detail matters more than extent
scale band region assumed from 'mapa gigantesco'; if the smallest thing that matters is animal-sized, the band drops to block and the extent has to be cut

open_questions.ask: What's the smallest thing you want to be able to make out in this world - undergrowth and props an animal's size, individual trees and riverbanks, whole forests and river courses, or coastlines and mountain ranges?
How should the rivers behave for the animals - something they swim straight across, a barrier that splits the map into separate territories, or a barrier with a few shallow crossings?
Which animals should the map be built around - forest predators like wolves and bears, hoofed herd animals like deer, big cats, or a mix of all of them? It sets the size of the dens and the trails.

captured: controllable animals (routed to mechanics as avatars, not scene)
walk / run / hit / jump joystick controls (mechanics)

notes_for_us: The prompt is entirely in Portuguese and neither skill says which language the emitted text should be written in. I wrote English, which will read oddly if the handoff is ever shown back to this user.

The universal six cover landform, water, settlement, islands and population but not vegetation cover. 'Varias florestas e vegetacoes' is the biggest thing in this prompt and step 2's search order runs out at id: null for it.

'Ultra realista ... como na vida real' is a theme and a whole-build constraint at once. Theme is free text so the words pass through, but nothing tells a later step that photoreal texture is a hard requirement rather than dressing - and on Roblox that is the sort of thing worth flagging before the render.

layout-intake tells me to offer the extent/detail split when both cannot be honoured, but with no user to answer, the trade-off can only land in notes. There is no field that records 'the frame cannot hold what was asked', so a downstream reader sees a confident region band instead.
